_comment: Every conversion constant the savings engine uses, with the basis it rests
on. They are here and not in code because each one is an assumption about
the world that a user may disagree with, and because an assessment has to
reproduce years later under the config version it was computed with.
A unit or period absent from these tables is UNSCORED, never guessed.

month.basis: a monthly figure is already monthly

week.basis: 52 weeks / 12 months; assumes pay every week of the year

day.basis: 261 working days / 12 months; assumes full-time, no unpaid leave

hour.basis: 40 hours x 52 weeks / 12 months; assumes a full-time schedule the posting did not state

pay_range_end.basis: the lower end of a published range is the part the employer commits to; using the midpoint or the top reports a salary nobody offered

_comment: T = stipend + allowances + visa-capped work income. A waiver reduces the
cost side and never the income side: a waived tuition fee is money not
spent, not money received, and adding it to income would report a
scholarship as paying a salary it does not pay.
scholarship.default_arrangement_basis: a scholarship is held at the institution unless the scheme says otherwise, so living costs are read where the institution is

work_income.zero_basis: work income counts only when both the permitted hours and an hourly wage figure are on file. Unverified work income is zero, which understates the funding rather than inventing a job the visa may not allow

_unscored_policy: Net savings is a number only when pay, tax and every required cost line
resolved. An incomplete cost list does not produce a smaller cost — it
produces a larger apparent saving, which is the direction that makes
somebody move country for a job that does not pay for itself.
